comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA for new bar use (Type 47) and outdoor activity area not at the front at 739–741 Valencia (144 m), NCT-VALENCIA district. Filed December 2010, approved April 2011 in ~4 months. This is a use decision combining bar and outdoor seating approvals.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A bar plus non-front outdoor area in a nearby NCT district (Valencia) was approved in 4 months in 2010–2011, demonstrating that outdoor seating paired with a full bar can pass Commission review when the outdoor space is not at the street front and the concept fits neighborhood character.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a written answer from San Francisco Planning on whether § 249.60(c)(3) applies to a Bona Fide Eating Place and whether the parking-lot outdoor area meets § 202.2(a)(7) limits.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a Letter of Determination or schedule a pre-application meeting with the Zoning Administrator. Describe the existing restaurant, the proposed enlargement from 1,464 sq ft to 3,227 sq ft, the parking-lot outdoor seating with beer-and-wine service closing at 10 pm, and ask: (1) Does Planning Code § 249.60(c)(3) requiring CU for expansion of a liquor establishment apply to a Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place, given that subsection (c) excludes such restaurants from the liquor establishment definition? (2) Does the parking-lot outdoor area meet every limit of § 202.2(a)(7) (ground level, 9 am–10 pm, not a Bar, seated only, alcohol dispensed inside or by wait staff at the seat) to avoid needing a CU? Submit the site plan showing the parking lot location and the proposed seating layout.

filing_playbook.action: Conduct the required Section 311 neighborhood notification: mail notice to property owners and occupants within 300 feet and post notice at the site for 30 days.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Planning will provide the notification packet with mailing labels and the poster template. Mail the notice and post the yellow poster at the site where it is visible to pedestrians. The 30-day comment period runs from the date of mailing and posting; Planning will not schedule the hearing until the comment period closes. Hold an informal community meeting if neighbors request one, and document your outreach and any neighbor concerns addressed.

filing_playbook.action: Register your San Francisco business and obtain a Business Account Number (BAN) from the Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector if not already registered.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The registration fee is tiered by gross receipts (for example $55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k, $625 at $1–1.5M for 2026–27, each plus a $4 state fee). Obtain it immediately after entity formation.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a Health Permit to Operate after the DPH final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans and a certified food safety manager is on staff.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online at least one month before opening with your BAN, LIN and EIN. The FY2026–27 fee is $470 for the Permit to Operate application (includes initial inspection) and $0 annual license fee for restaurants and bars for 2026–28. Schedule the final inspection when construction is complete, the hood is installed and the equipment is in place. At the inspection, have proof that at least one owner or employee holds a California Food Protection Manager certificate (valid 5 years) and that all food-handling employees have Food Handler Cards (valid 3 years). The permit is issued after the inspection passes; you cannot serve the public before it is issued.

timeline_cost.notes: The day and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization, ABC license review (if a modification is needed), and the Health permit to operate, which are the approvals in the entitlement path. The 120–300 day range is the time to approval when those approvals are granted, measured from filing the CUA to Commission approval (comparable outdoor CUAs in NCT districts took 7–268 days for approved cases, N=6), plus ABC review if triggered (60–120 days per the catalog), plus health permit processing (14–45 days per the catalog). The cost range of $3,100–$15,000 is the CUA application fee, which varies with construction cost; the 2023–24 base CUA fee was approximately $2,747 and is CPI-adjusted annually to roughly $3,150 in 2026–27, rising to $15,000 when paired with significant tenant improvements. ABC Type 41 fees ($1,000–$1,600) and health permit fees ($470 application plus $828–$2,207 plan check) are not included because the ABC license is already held (so no new license fee, though a modification may cost less than a new license) and health/building permits are needed regardless of the CUA outcome. Building permit, plan check, and construction costs are excluded because they depend on the scope of tenant improvements, not the CUA itself. The ranges assume approval; they are not times or costs to a denial or a withdrawal.

records_summary: The property at 2214 Mission St is in the Mission Street NCT zoning district, where restaurants are conditional uses. The site sits inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which requires conditional use authorization for any restaurant in this sub-area and imposes operating conditions on all liquor establishments. The immediate block is extremely dense: 33 food and drink businesses within 500 feet, 14 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet, and 50 within 1,000 feet. Most significantly, this exact address has a withdrawn CUA from 2010–2012 for outdoor seating on an adjacent parking lot—the same concept now proposed—which was filed but withdrawn after nearly two years without a decision.
